_README: An example of the manifest that lives NEXT TO the artwork, not in this
repository: copy it to the folder holding the original files, rename it to
patterns.manifest.json, and list what the folder holds. Then run
npm run catalog:import -- "<that folder>". docs/ADDING_PATTERNS.md has the
whole flow in Thai and English.
Keys underscored like this one are ignored. Every other key is checked, and
a mistake is reported with the id of the entry it is in.
THE ID IS THE IDENTITY. It names the files the site serves and the entry in
the catalog. Re-export a drawing under any file name, keep its id, and the
designs people have already made keep their pattern. Change an id and it is
a different pattern: the old one is deleted, and a saved design that used it
loses that layer. Remove an entry and the same happens.
The import never touches the originals and never copies them into the repo.

patterns._comment: A repeating tile: the ordinary case.
_repeatUnits: How wide one repeat prints, in the units every product mockup is
measured in: a whole product is 1000 across, a cotton shawl's cloth is
660 x 464, a handkerchief 580 x 580. 500 is a large print, about 1.3
repeats across a shawl. The height follows the picture's proportions.
Changing it later resizes designs people have already saved, so it is
patterns._tags: Searchable words. "community" is added for you.

_comment: A placement pattern: one drawing that fills the print area once,
instead of a surface that repeats. It has no repeat size — the print
area decides how big it is — and its edges never have to meet, so the
import's seam warnings mean nothing for it.
Everything an entry may carry, in one place.
restrictTo keeps a pattern off products it was not drawn for: name
product lines (fabric, leaf, gift, drinkware), or single products by
id (shawl-cotton, handkerchief, leaf-plate, ...), or both — a product
qualifies on either. Leave it out and the pattern prints on
everything, which is what all seven do today.
